summary_for_children: Al-Mu'minun begins by describing successful believers: humble in prayer, avoiding idle talk, giving charity and keeping promises. It reminds us how Allah created us and sends rain in just measure.
environment_concept: Terraces of the successful believers: a quiet stepped terrace (23:2-3), rain held in great basins (23:18), palms and vines (23:19), a great olive tree (23:20) and an empty shipyard (23:27).
architecture_and_scenery: Terraced garden with palm and vine rows, a single great olive tree on a slope, a reservoir, and a ship-building yard at its lower edge.

palette.atmosphere: Calm, the sound of water held in reservoirs

depiction_rules: No prophet, person or representation of Allah is shown. Unseen realities are never pictured. Interactive activities are labelled as adaptations.

unique_world.visual_theme: Four open rooms round a courtyard: a hall with a door and a high shelf, a prayer corner, a window room with a plant and a bell, and a store room with a giving jar

primary_mechanic.text: One day in a home with a running clock: a kept parcel handed back when the neighbour knocks, a promise to water the plant when the bell rings (not before), the prayer corner cleared by the chime, and giving from the jar (23:1-11). A missed time comes round again. Each room comes alive when its quality is kept.

secondary_activities: the ship (23:27, read only, linked to the Ark in Surah Hud)
unique_world.narrative_structure: The sign at the gate, the day at home, then three readings
world_assets: prayer rug, toys and toy box
window plant, tap, watering can and bell
environment_behaviour: a day clock with things coming due shown on the status line
rooms brighten, light up and flower when kept
the plant droops when the promise is missed
unique_world.learning_objective: Practise the qualities of 23:1-11 as keeping things at their time: trusts, promises, prayer and giving

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Qualities of Believers
story_library.children_narration: The Quran describes believers who pray sincerely, keep their promises, and avoid harmful behavior. It reminds us how human life begins and retells parts of the stories of Nuh and Musa. Faith is not only something we say; it also changes how we act.

world_idea.title: The Living Home of Good Character
world_idea.description: A home and community environment that changes as children practice trustworthiness, care, and responsibility. A separate ark chapter introduces Nuh's account.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: The library suggests an ark chapter. 23:27 does mention the ship and the pairs, but the ark game already lives in Hud. Surah 23 gets a reading and a link, not a second ark game.
